record.paper_title: Global results on rational systems in the plane, part 1
record.original_question: For each of the 31 planar rational systems that may be cooperative in some parameter range and nowhere competitive, determine the exact parameter region where the system is cooperative, determine whether the cooperative-system monotonicity hypotheses corresponding to Theorem 3.16 or Theorem 3.17 are satisfied, and determine the global character of all solutions. The 31 systems are (35,40), (35,46), (36,40), (36,46), (45,46); (k,l) with k <= l, k in {34,46}, and l in {34,35,36,40,45,46,47,48,49}; and (k,l) with k <= l, k in {25,40}, and l in {34,35,36,45,46,47,48,49}. The relevant Theorem 3.16 hypothesis is a one-step mixed-direction monotonicity implication for cooperative systems, yielding eventual monotonicity of both component sequences; the relevant Theorem 3.17 hypothesis is the analogous two-step condition yielding eventual monotonicity of the four even and odd component subsequences.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider planar systems of rational difference equations of the form
    x_{n+1} = (α₁ + β₁ x_n + γ₁ y_n)/(A₁ + B₁ x_n + C₁ y_n),
    y_{n+1} = (α₂ + β₂ x_n + γ₂ y_n)/(A₂ + B₂ x_n + C₂ y_n),
with nonnegative parameters and nonnegative initial conditions (x₀, y₀) such that the denominators never vanish and the iterates remain nonnegative. Each numerator/denominator pair (k, l) refers to one of the 49 distinct rational expressions obtained by selecting a subset of {1, x, y} for the numerator and a subset of {1, x, y} for the denominator (with arbitrary nonnegative coefficients), enumerated in a fixed standard order in which:
 • k labels the right-hand side of the x-equation,
 • l labels the right-hand side of the y-equation,
 • the convention k ≤ l is taken whenever both equations are interchangeable.

A planar map T(x,y) = (f(x,y), g(x,y)) on a domain in the nonnegative quadrant is called cooperative if ∂f/∂y ≥ 0 and ∂g/∂x ≥ 0 throughout the domain, and competitive if these partial derivatives are ≤ 0. The 31 systems listed below are precisely those (out of the 49×49 possibilities subject to k ≤ l where appropriate) which are cooperative for some open region of parameter space and never competitive on any region of parameter space:

  (35,40), (35,46), (36,40), (36,46), (45,46);
  (k,l) with k ≤ l, k ∈ {34, 46}, l ∈ {34, 35, 36, 40, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49};
  (k,l) with k ≤ l, k ∈ {25, 40}, l ∈ {34, 35, 36, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49}.

For a cooperative planar map T, consider the following two hypotheses governing eventual monotonicity of orbits (x_n, y_n) = T^n(x₀, y₀):

(H1) One-step mixed-direction monotonicity: for every (x,y) in the domain,
    [f(x,y) ≥ x and g(x,y) ≤ y]  or  [f(x,y) ≤ x and g(x,y) ≥ y]
  implies the analogous inequalities at (f(x,y), g(x,y)). Under (H1), both sequences {x_n} and {y_n} are eventually monotonic.

(H2) Two-step analogue of (H1) applied to T², ensuring that the four subsequences {x_{2n}}, {x_{2n+1}}, {y_{2n}}, {y_{2n+1}} are eventually monotonic.

For each of the 31 systems above, solve the following three tasks:
 (a) Determine explicitly the region in parameter space on which the system is cooperative.
 (b) Determine on which subregion of that cooperative region hypothesis (H1) holds, and on which subregion hypothesis (H2) holds.
 (c) Determine the global character of all nonnegative solutions: the set of equilibria and periodic solutions, their local stability, basins of attraction, existence of invariant manifolds, and global asymptotic behavior of every orbit, as a function of the parameters.
artifact.status_search_result: No publication was located that resolves, even for all 31 listed systems collectively, the three-part question of cooperative parameter region, verification of the monotonicity hypotheses (H1)/(H2), and full global dynamics. Related follow-up work by Camouzis, Ladas, and collaborators on partial cases of planar rational systems exists, but a comprehensive resolution of this open problem does not appear in the literature, so it is treated as still open.

status_evidence.title: Global results on rational systems in the plane, part 1
status_evidence.snippet: Camouzis-Ladas paper posing open problems on planar rational systems including cooperative cases.
status_evidence.claim: The originating work poses the open problem of global analysis of these 31 candidate cooperative planar rational systems.

status_evidence.title: Patterns of Boundedness of Rational Systems in the Plane
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work addressing partial aspects (boundedness) of planar rational systems.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up literature treats partial aspects (e.g., boundedness, competitive cases) but does not give a complete global classification for all 31 cooperative-candidate systems.
